outcomeNote: Shmuel's definition is displaced by Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak's

segments.he: מֵיתִיבִי: לֹא כׇּל הַבּוֹרוֹת הַקָּרוֹת הִתִּירוּ, אֶלָּא זוֹ בִּלְבַד. וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ ״שֶׁהִקְרוּ דְּבָרִים עָלֶיהָ״, מַאי ״זוֹ בִּלְבַד״?
segments.en: The Gemara «raises an objection» from a baraita: «They did not permit all Heker wells, but only this one. And if you say» it was named because it is a cistern «with regard to which they put forward arguments» and permitted it, «what is» the meaning of Heker wells in the plural, and what does «only this one» mean? If it was named because of a particular announcement, how could other wells, about which no announcement was issued, bear the same name?

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: בְּאֵר מַיִם חַיִּים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כְּהָקִיר בַּיִר מֵימֶיהָ וְגוֹ׳״.
segments.en: «Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:» The term Heker well denotes «a well of living water, as it is stated: “As a well keeps its water fresh» [«hakir»], so she keeps fresh her wickedness” (Jeremiah 6:7), i.e., it is a well of spring water.

segments.he: גּוּפָא: לֹא כׇּל הַבּוֹרוֹת הַקָּרוֹת הִתִּירוּ, אֶלָּא זוֹ בִּלְבַד. וּכְשֶׁעָלוּ בְּנֵי הַגּוֹלָה חָנוּ עָלֶיהָ, וּנְבִיאִים שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶן הִתִּירוּ לָהֶן. וְלֹא נְבִיאִים שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶן, אֶלָּא מִנְהַג אֲבוֹתָם בִּידֵיהֶם.
segments.en: Returning to «the matter itself,» the Gemara cites the above baraita in full: «They did not permit all Heker wells, but only this one. And when the exiles ascended» from Babylonia, «they encamped by it, and the prophets among them,» Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi, «permitted» it «to them. And it was not» really «the prophets among them» who permitted them to draw water from this well on a Festival, «but» rather, it was «a customary practice» that was handed down «to them from their forefathers,» a practice the prophets permitted them to continue.
